names_for.catalogue_side: A1 데이터 마켓플레이스 (A1 Data Marketplace); '판매 중인 데이터' / Datasets
names_for.custom_side: 커스텀 데이터 / 맞춤형 데이터셋 구축 ('Build custom DATA'); 신규 데이터 구축

operator_role.note: Buyer contracts with Crowdworks, which manages and sells partner data; the buyer contract itself is not public, so 'licensor of record' wording was not seen.

economics_model.note: Own-collected datasets sold as principal; partner data sold under a contract-specific revenue split.

who_pays_fee.note: Crowdworks' cut comes out of sale proceeds via the contractual split; no buyer-side fee published.

supply_models.note: No evidence found either way that client-commissioned project data is relisted.

public_prices.note: No price on any listing examined (robot arm, senior interviews, SERICEO, Korean architecture, Vietnam, doctor-patient dialogue); quotes only on inquiry.

licence_model.note: Scope of use and price are set per inquiry and written into each customer contract; no standard licence text is published.

exclusivity_offered.note: Exclusive data is offered only as new collection on request (Vietnam listing); no evidence on exclusivity for listed stock.

sample_mechanics.note: Most listings carry a sample-request form; the newest 2026 listings examined (robot arm, Vietnam, senior interviews, architecture, SERICEO) had none.

versioning.note: Listings state update cycles (monthly, negotiable) but nothing on versions or what past buyers receive.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Public pages give only assertions (voluntary parental participation on one listing, blanket no-legal-dispute claim) and are silent on the senior-interview listing; what the buyer contract delivers is not public.

contributor_pay_model.note: 145 global teleoperators contributed; how they were paid is not published.

quality_evidence.note: Operator verification is vendor-stated; no independent check found.

Q1.answer: Crowdworks gives only company-wide customer counts (567 companies, 70% of KOSPI top-30) and dataset sizes; no A1 sales volume, unit or buyer mix is published.

Q2.answer: Holders list through Crowdworks, which signs a partner contract, sells under its own contract with the buyer, tells the seller which company is buying and shares revenue at a contracted ratio.

Q3.answer: Inventory is Crowdworks' own collection (e.g. 145-operator teleoperation data, physical-AI lab data) plus partner holders' data (a Vietnamese conglomerate affiliate, a photo archive also on stock sites, SERICEO), all said to pass Crowdworks inspection.

Q5.answer: The buyer contracts with Crowdworks, not the holder; Crowdworks asserts all data is free of copyright or other legal-dispute risk, but no warranty or indemnity text is public.

Q7.answer: Only assertions: data free of legal disputes, properly licensed, 'ethically built', and on one children's listing voluntary parental participation; the senior-interview listing withholds face-visible originals behind an NDA and says nothing on consent.

Q8.answer: Usage terms and price are set per scope of use in each customer contract; Crowdworks issues blockchain transaction certificates via its A1 Data Exchange; no exclusivity, audit or fingerprinting terms are published.

Q9.answer: No checkout: a 'data purchase inquiry' leads to a quote and a contract between customer and Crowdworks, priced by scope of use and data source; sellers get a revenue share at a contract-specific ratio.

Q10.answer: A listing is a public page with a spec table (count, type, collection method, format, metadata, update cycle), some sold as quantity-expandable licence products; nothing is published on revisions, orders or entitlements.

Q11.answer: Listings show descriptive specs and most carry a sample-request form; trust rests on Crowdworks' own inspection claims, per-demonstration quality scores and blockchain transaction certificates; the homepage FAQ and testimonials are template filler.

Q12.answer: A1 sits alongside Crowdworks' core bespoke data-construction business: listings and the homepage offer to restructure listed data, collect new data (exclusive or not) or process buyer-owned data.
